source.title: Demon: Improved Neural Network Training With Momentum Decay
source.authors: John Chen; Cameron R. Wolfe; Zhaoqi Li; Anastasios Kyrillidis

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance of Adam and SGDM across training schedules and settings, bearing on whether adaptive optimization performs worse than SGD. Its focus is momentum decay, not a direct reproduction of the cited optimizer comparison.
record.gate_note: The reported comparisons concern held-out generalization error, perplexity, loss, or task scores under different optimizer schedules. No random-label memorization, width sweep, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparison, batch-size comparison, dropout intervention, sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal is tested.
record.test_reason: Tables 3–4 permit matched Adam-versus-SGDM comparisons of held-out performance, testing V4. The extracted rows instead compare schedules within an optimizer. Tuning includes momentum and weight decay, so this is not a replication of V4's restricted tuning protocol.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but understates the main conclusion: the authors report that Demon has the highest Top-1 and Top-3 finish rates across 28 settings, applies effectively to both Adam and SGDM, and improves robustness to hyperparameter tuning relative to step decay. They also report no noteworthy ImageNet difference from step decay.
record.recipe_differences: Tests a proposed momentum-decay schedule against learning-rate and momentum schedules across model and dataset settings; not a reproduction of the optimizer generalization comparisons named in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by dataset, architecture, epoch budget, optimizer, and schedule. The authors report no worthwhile result difference between Demon and learning-rate step decay on ImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Demon changes held-out performance relative to other schedules within Adam or SGDM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum-decay schedules can change optimizer performance and sensitivity to hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Demon changes VAE loss and NCSN sample quality relative to optimizer baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer schedules affect generative-model loss and generated-sample quality.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: The text says ImageNet runs showed no results worth noting between learning-rate step decay and Demon. The BERT comparison tunes only learning rate. The NCSN comparison reports an inception score and notes qualitative image differences, rather than classification generalization error. Table 6 does not provide uncertainty values.
record.rows_left_out: Optimizer-schedule table results beyond the selected Adam/SGDM step-schedule versus Demon comparisons were left out, including alternative schedules and adaptive optimizer baselines in Tables 3 and 4, because the extracted rows prioritize direct Adam/SGDM comparisons and the mixed outcomes. Table 7's effective-learning-rate-adjusted SGD comparison is not included; it compares Demon with an SGD approximation rather than the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison named in V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning restriction; equal or better adaptive training performance; switching Adam to SGD. AdamW baselines are included, but do not isolate decoupling weight decay under matched schedules.
Batch-size interventions and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions; fixed dropout in the PTB model is not a test.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.

missing.what: Matched Adam-versus-SGDM comparisons on CIFAR10 and STL10, separately for each epoch budget and for step decay and Demon. The component values are extracted, but no row records the comparison that tests V4.
Matched Adam-versus-SGDM comparisons on VGG16/CIFAR100, separately for 150 and 300 epochs and step decay and Demon, preserving the changing optimizer ordering.
Matched Adam-versus-SGDM comparisons on word-level PTB, separately for 25 and 39 epochs and step decay and Demon.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Verdicts use explicitly identified comparisons from the supplied text because the extracted rows encode within-optimizer schedule effects. A cannot_determine state here concerns the row's ability to establish a claim version, not whether its schedule difference is readable. Alternative schedules and adaptive baselines already declared in rows_left_out are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
The study compares Adam and SGDM under schedules, but does not test the cited studies' broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language-model claim.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.

relationships.condition: ResNet20/CIFAR10 and Wide ResNet/STL10, matched step schedules and matched Demon schedules
relationships.reason: From Table 3, requiring new comparison rows: Adam has higher error at every reported budget. Step-schedule errors are 10.47/8.75/8.55 versus SGDM's 8.82/8.43/7.32 on CIFAR10, and 23.85/19.63/18.29 versus 22.42/17.20/14.51 on STL10. This holds despite tuning beyond learning rates and schedules.
relationships.display_finding: Reported error favored SGDM at every tested budget with both schedule types despite broader tuning, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.reason: Table 3 shows higher Adam error than SGDM at every reported budget for both step and Demon schedules on these datasets. This supports the performance ordering under the study's broader tuning.

relationships.condition: PTB word-level LSTM, 25 and 39 epochs, matched step schedules and matched Demon schedules
relationships.reason: From Table 4, requiring new comparison rows: step-schedule Adam perplexities are 98.79 and 99.69 versus SGDM's 81.67 and 82.02; Demon Adam gives 104.60 and 107.07 versus Demon SGDM's 82.66 and 84.84. Adam's possible advantage on word-level models does not appear here.
relationships.display_finding: Reported test perplexity favored SGDM at both epoch budgets with both schedule types, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: VGG16/CIFAR100, schedule and epoch budget varied
relationships.reason: From Table 4, requiring new comparison rows: with step decay Adam has lower mean error at 150 epochs, 29.40 versus 30.09, and nearly equal error at 300 epochs, 27.75 versus 27.83. With Demon, Adam is slightly worse at 150 epochs, 28.84 versus 28.67, but better at 300, 27.11 versus 27.69. The ordering depends on schedule and budget under broader tuning.
relationships.display_finding: The reported optimizer rankings by error vary with the schedule (step decay or Demon) and training budget, but these comparisons remain unverified.
